The inflow was higher than Rs 29,329 crore recorded in August, according to data released by the Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI) on Monday.
Among equity categories, small-cap funds attracted the highest net inflow of Rs 9,039 crore, followed by mid-cap funds at Rs 7,835 crore. Large-cap funds, meanwhile, saw net inflows of Rs 860 crore during the month.
" Equity inflows jumped sharply in a month when markets were under pressure. Much of that reflects the lasting faith Indian investors have in equities as one of the best long-term routes to wealth creation. articles.title: Beauty comes at a festive premium
articles.summary: New Delhi: Salons and services apps have doubled prices over last festive season amid sharp surge in demand for services such as dandiya luxe and garba glows to Durga deity looks and Navratri queens. Executives attributed the increase in prices to a combination of a surge in costs of key ingredients such as palm oil, and glass and plastic bottles and aerosols by 25-30% year-on-year on account of the West Asia war, pricing power and the withdrawal of input tax credit on salons last year.“As we speak, consumers are booking packages for new looks for each of the seven or nine days of Navratri and dandiya,” said CK Kumaravel, co-founder of Naturals Salons. “Prices have doubled over last year, since with the unexpected surge in demand, the industry is exercising high pricing power,” he said.Also Read: Festive cheer shifts beyond metros as consumer brands bet big on small-town IndiaOn Urban Company’s salon luxe, prices have touched Rs 5,000-plus, with services including make-up from global beauty brands such as Casmara and Mac.Since this is peak festive season with surge in demand specially from small towns, salons such as Madonna, Looks, Gitanjali and BBlunt have hiked prices to cash in on the season.“Further, the consequences of the withdrawal of input tax credit (ITC) late last year on salon chains, fitness centres, gyms and yoga clubs, despite reduction in GST slabs from 18% to 5%, are being passed on to the consumer,” said an executive at a beauty services platform. He requested not to be identified.“As salon operators and owners, we pay tax on equipment and raw materials. In the absence of refunds of input tax credit, our overall tax liability remains high and neutralises the reduction of GST on services,” he added.The West Asia war, which led to supply disruptions and spiked the prices of packaging materials, further hurt margins of the entire personal care sector. Crude-linked petroleum derivatives, and speciality chemicals imported from West Asia are key ingredients for cosmetics and beauty products.Also Read: Retailers, quick commerce companies limit sugar rush amid stock painHindustan Unilever’s Lakme Salon estimated in a report that India’s beauty salon market would reach $22.99 billion by 2033, at a CAGR of 7.85% during 2024 – 2033. This compares to a market valued at US $ 11.65 billion in 2024. The report attributes the double-digit growth the industry is witnessing to changing lifestyles, increasing disposable incomes, and consumers opting for premium experiences.Chains are also pushing their private labels on other platforms.At-home salon and wellness platform Yes Madam said in a statement last week that it has expanded its Korean skin and hair care range Sokora across D2C and e-commerce channels. Cofounder Aditya Arya, Yes Madam, said in a statement: “We focused on making the range convenient for everyday use … at home as well.”

articles.title: Mutual funds close in on FPIs in Indian equity ownership
articles.summary: Mumbai: Indian mutual funds are closing in on foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) in their share of domestic equities, with the ownership gap narrowing to around 230 basis points, the lowest on record.The share of mutual funds' holdings in Indian equities rose to a record 11.7% in September, while that of FPIs fell below 14%, according to NSDL data. The FPI share has declined from a record 20% in May 2021, while the mutual fund share has climbed from around 7% during the same period. In January, the mutual fund share was 11%.The contraction in the ownership gap is an outcome of record selling by foreign investors along with unabated purchases by domestic mutual funds thanks to the deluge of retail flows into their equity products.134880107"In every market, normally local investors dominate and the same trend is emerging in India," said Samir Arora, founder and fund manager at Helios Capital Management. "It is reasonable to expect that in the medium term local institutional investors will own more of the market than foreign investors."Read more: Weekly Market Outlook: Nifty snaps 8-week losing streak, but can bulls reclaim the crucial 200-week moving average?FPIs' total equity assets under custody stood at ₹66.18 lakh crore in September, the lowest since March 2026, compared with a record ₹77.96 lakh crore in September 2024, when FPIs accounted for around 16.4% of Indian equities.Read more: ET Alpha Wealth Summit 2.0: What do Shah Rukh Khan and SIFs have in common? Radhika Gupta explainsMeanwhile, mutual funds' equity assets stood at around ₹55.14 lakh crore, up from around ₹20 lakh crore in April 2022. The corpus doubled to around ₹40 lakh crore by January 2024 and crossed ₹50 lakh crore in October 2025."Over time, mutual funds, high-net-worth individuals and family offices collectively are likely to account for a larger share of the market," said Ritesh Jain, founder of Canada-based Pinetree Macro.The changing ownership pattern is more pronounced among Nifty 500 companies, where domestic institutional investors (DIIs) have overtaken FPIs. DII holdings rose for the 9th consecutive quarter to a record 21% in Q1FY27, while FPI holdings fell to 17%, according to a Motilal Oswal Financial Services note.Sector Ownership DynamicsThe changing composition of the Indian economy could also be influencing FPI investment patterns. Foreign investors, which have historically had significant exposure to banks and IT companies, are now looking beyond these established sectors.The decline in FPI ownership has been visible across several key sectors, including IT, FMCG, consumer services, realty and financials. But, the trend has not been uniform, with foreign investors increasing their holdings in capital goods, metals and mining, telecom, services and healthcare.A recovery in corporate earnings will be key to a return of foreign investor appetite for Indian equities at a time when Asian markets such as Taiwan and Korea are hogging the limelight, boosted by AI-centric investments."If earnings grow at around 14-15% annually and the currency depreciates by around 2-3% a year, the resulting return for foreign investors would still be around 12%," said Arora.

articles.title: Houthis widen threat to Saudi airspace
articles.summary: Sanaa: Yemen's Houthis issued a new threat to Saudi Arabia's airspace on Sunday after an attack on the kingdom's international airport in Riyadh killed 12 people and wounded hundreds.Saturday's attack, the deadliest on Saudi soil in more than a decade, was a sharp escalation in the Yemen war, where Riyadh backs the internationally recognised government against the Houthis, who captured swathes of Red Sea coastline in a lightning offensive last month.Also Read: Houthis' attack on Saudi's Riyadh airport kills 12, injures over 300 as conflict escalatesWhile the Houthis stopped short of claiming the strike, they threatened new attacks on the kingdom's airports, except for the holy cities of Mecca and Medina, warning passengers not to travel."The airports and airspace are exposed to targeting and constitute a theatre of operations for our forces," military spokesman Yahya Saree wrote on X.The strike came in a week when the group intensified its attacks on the Saudi capital's King Khalid International Airport, where three people were also killed on Thursday, as well as other key targets in the world's largest crude oil exporter.A spokesman for the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis in Yemen attributed Saturday's attack to the Iran-backed group, calling it a "full-fledged war crime".A diplomatic source also attributed the strike to a Houthi missile.The coalition vowed to respond, and on Sunday Houthi media reported that two Saudi strikes had targeted Sanaa governorate in Yemen, which is controlled by the Houthis.The assault on the Saudi capital's aviation hub drew condemnation from a UN special envoy and several world leaders including US President Donald Trump, who said it was "not acceptable" and that he was looking at joining Saudi strikes against the Houthis."We may. We're going to look at it. We just found out about the recent attack, so we'll make a decision," he told reporters at the White House.Four Saudi citizens were among those killed, as well as two Bangladeshis, one American, one Egyptian, one Jordanian, one Syrian, one Palestinian and one Sudanese, Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority said.It said some of the 309 wounded were in serious condition.Also Read: Tension spikes in West Asia as Saudi coalition threatens retaliation after deadly Houthi strike on Riyadh airportA Western diplomat based in Riyadh told AFP that the official number of injured did not appear to give a full picture of the aftermath.The number also does not seem to include those who sustained minor wounds, the diplomat said.- Operations suspended -Authorities suspended operations at the airport into Sunday, a senior aviation source told AFP, with air traffic monitor Flightradar24 saying the closure was extended until 2100 GMT.A second source working in the aviation sector who helps oversee flights to Riyadh confirmed the halt in operations "until further notice"."The information we have is... that some systems have been damaged -- the radar and communications equipment," the source told AFP, adding that runways also needed to be assessed.One passenger told AFP they witnessed a strike in the airport's domestic terminal."I was on gate 403," the witness said. "I saw 401 hit, I saw injured in front of my eyes. Everyone was running."The US, Canadian, German and Spanish embassies in Saudi Arabia warned their citizens to avoid the airport.A senior Western diplomat told AFP that several embassies were banning their staff from using the airport "over the next week".The Saudi-led coalition also announced on Saturday evening the fall of a projectile near Dammam airport, in the east of the kingdom.The US embassy in Saudi Arabia on Sunday said staff working in the kingdom would now be required to request permission to use airports in the cities of Dammam and Jeddah, days after a similar order was issued for Riyadh.- Doctor call-up -The Riyadh attack prompted health officials to activate a rare mass call-up of doctors, a medical source said.Schools in Riyadh switched to remote learning for the second time in a month, according to emails seen by AFP that were received by parents.European Union chief Ursula von der Leyen called the strike a "dangerous escalation", while Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif condemned the "heinous attack" and Jordan called it "brutal".It was the deadliest attack in the kingdom since May 2015, when a suicide bombing by the Islamic State jihadist group killed 21 worshippers in the eastern Qatif governorate. It also came on the eve of Saudi Arabia's high-profile convention and entertainment season.Riyadh usually hosts a packed calendar of events, including its flagship investment conference drawing foreign leaders and business titans.The WPC Energy Congress kicked off in Riyadh on Sunday after being delayed due to the outbreak of the US-Iran war in February.Saudi Arabia leads an international coalition that has supported Yemen's government militarily since 2015.In Yemen, Saudi-supported government forces were advancing against the Houthis in areas the group captured last month around the Bab al-Mandab strait, a key chokepoint for Red Sea oil and cargo shipping, military sources told AFP on Saturday.The Houthis claimed to have repelled them.The Yemeni government last week announced a counter-offensive to retake Houthi territory.Claims by the warring parties have been impossible to independently verify, with the situation moving fast on the ground and access for journalists difficult.

NTPC invites bids for 26% stake in industrial co-generation projects
articles.summary:
NTPC Limited, India's largest integrated power utility, has invited Expressions of Interest (EOI) from Commercial and Industrial (C&I) entities interested in taking 26 per cent equity in co-generation projects.
The initiative aims to explore opportunities to develop co-generation facilities to meet industrial requirements for steam and electricity, along with integrated power supply solutions based on coal, renewable energy and Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), the power PSU said in a statement.
With industries increasingly focusing on energy security, cost optimisation and sustainability, co-generation offers an opportunity to enhance overall energy efficiency by producing steam and electricity through an integrated system.
The proposed initiative seeks to address the diverse requirements of industries with reliable, economical and sustainable energy solutions through long-term power supply arrangements.

articles.title: Indian-Americans back favourable candidates in US midterms elections
articles.summary:
Indian-Americans are seeking not just a share in power in the US by getting elected as lawmakers but are also supporting others sympathetic to their cause in the November 3 midterm elections.
The outgoing US House of Representatives have six members of Indian origin, but the number is likely to shrink to four with Raja Krishnamoorthi from Illinois and Shri Thanedar from Michigan failing to clear the primaries.
Indian-American Congresspersons Ro Khanna (California-17), Pramila Jayapal (Washington-7), Ami Bera (California-3) and Suhas Subramanyam (Virginia-10) are up for re-election.
The US midterm elections are held halfway through a president's four-year term to elect all 435 members of the House of Representatives, the lower house of Congress, and about one-third of the 100-member Senate, the upper house.

PM Modi holds roadshow in Chennai, to launch projects worth ₹13,000 crore
articles.summary:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi arrived here on Sunday to lay the foundation stone for projects and also dedicate projects worth over Rs 13,000 crore.
Upon his arrival at the airport by 11 am, Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay accorded him a warm welcome.
PM Modi briefly held a roadshow and waved at the BJP workers and supporters who lined up behind barricades near the airport to welcome him.
As Modi's motorcade moved out of the airport, a serpentine queue of BJP workers and supporters waiting on roadsides waved to him and raised "Bharat Mata Ki Jai," slogans.
Tamil Nadu BJP accorded him a warm welcome by also holding cultural programmes like traditional dance shows on specially earmarked spaces on the roadside near the airport.
